CHAP. IV. 
 
  The brazen altar, sea and lavers, ver. 1-5.   The golden candlesticks and tables, ver. 7, 8.   The doors overlaid with brass, the vessels of the altar,   and other brass work, ver. 9-18.   The golden altar of incense with its appurtenances, ver. 19-22.
V. 7. Their form-The old form which God prescribed to Moses.
V. 8. Ten tables-Whereon the shew-bread was set, ver.
. Perhaps each of these had twelve loaves on it.  As the house was enlarged, so was the provision.

V. 16. His father-He is so called because Solomon usually called him by that name out of that great respect which he bare to him for his excellent art and service which he did for him: it being usual to call great artists and inventors of things by this name.
V. 20. The manner-According to the prescription of God to Moses.
V. 22. Of gold-In part; they were made of wood, but covered with golden plates.
